evidence: Varr. RR 1.2.10: ut videant pinacothēcās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek πινακοθήκη, a room or building for pictures: in a rich Roman house (Vitruvius) or open to the public. The classical word is also Traupman’s and Morgan–Owens’s for an art gallery.

phrases.latin: celeberrimī pictōrēs, quōrum tabulae pinacothēcās implent
phrases.english: the most famous painters, whose pictures fill the galleries

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. museum: gallery (art). John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 173.
